title: The 10 Best Pry Bars
subtitle: Ranked from live Amazon data — best-sellers, real ratings, honest trade-offs.
intro: We pulled the best-selling pry bars on Amazon: flat bars for trim and nails, handled bars with strike caps, indexing-head bars for auto work, and long wrecking bars for demolition. Each one is scored on a 100-point scale built from its star rating, review volume and four features: a multi-piece set, a steel strike cap, a lifetime warranty and US manufacture. Pick by the job first; a 7-inch flat bar and a 36-inch wrecking bar don't do the same work.

buyers_guide.q: What size pry bar do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Match the length to the force and the space. A 7 to 10 inch flat bar handles trim, molding and small nails. A 12 to 18 inch bar covers most general prying. A 24 to 36 inch bar or wrecking bar is for demolition and lifting heavy things, where leverage matters more than reach into tight spots.

buyers_guide.q: Flat bar, handled bar or wrecking bar?
buyers_guide.a: Flat bars are thin and slip into gaps, so they suit trim, flooring and nail pulling. Handled bars have a grip and usually a strike cap, so you can hammer the tip into place and pry hard without hurting your hands. Gooseneck wrecking bars are long, heavy demolition tools with a hook for spikes.

buyers_guide.q: What does an indexing pry bar do?
buyers_guide.a: Its head pivots and locks at several angles, so you can pry around an obstruction or from the side. Mechanics use them on suspension, exhaust and engine parts. The GEARWRENCH bars on this page lock in up to 14 positions.

buyers_guide.q: Is a strike cap worth having?
buyers_guide.a: Yes, if you'll drive the tip in with a hammer. A steel cap takes the blow instead of the plastic grip. On the best designs, like the Mayhew set here, the cap sits directly on the steel shaft.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use a screwdriver as a pry bar?
buyers_guide.a: You can, but you'll likely bend the shaft or chip the tip, and a slipping screwdriver is an easy way to cut yourself. A $13 to $15 flat bar is made for the job.
